paras: Dopasia buettikoferi, also known commonly as the Bornean glass snake and Buettikofer's glass lizard, is a species of lizard in the family Anguidae. The species is native to Indonesia and Malaysia on the island of Borneo.
The specific name, buettikoferi, is in honor of Swiss zoologist Johann Büttikofer.
The preferred natural habitat of D. buettikoferi is forest, at altitudes of 300–1,600 m (980–5,250 ft).

D. buettikoferi has no external limbs, and its tail is three times as long as its head and body. The holotype has a snout-to-vent length (SVL) of 12.5 cm (4.9 in) and a tail length of 37.5 cm (14.8 in). It is brown dorsally and yellowish ventally. There is a dark brown line on each side of the body and tail.
D. buettikoferi is diurnal, terrestrial, and semi-fossorial.
D. buettikoferi preys predominately upon insects.
